questions.q: A patient with primary ovarian failure has reduced circulating oestradiol. Which pituitary hormone is expected to rise because ovarian negative feedback has fallen?
questions.explain: Oestradiol and inhibin normally exert negative feedback on the hypothalamus and pituitary. Ovarian failure reduces this feedback, so gonadotropins—particularly FSH—rise.

questions.q: Which hormone released by Sertoli cells selectively suppresses pituitary FSH secretion?
questions.explain: Sertoli cells secrete inhibin B, which provides negative feedback on the anterior pituitary to reduce FSH secretion. Testosterone from Leydig cells provides broader negative feedback through the hypothalamic-pituitary axis.

questions.q: A man has selective failure of Leydig-cell function. Which endocrine change is most likely?
options: Reduced FSH with increased inhibin B
questions.explain: Leydig cells respond to LH by synthesising testosterone. Primary Leydig-cell failure lowers testosterone and reduces negative feedback, so LH generally rises.

questions.q: Which ovarian cell type is primarily stimulated by LH to produce androgens that can be aromatised by granulosa cells?
questions.explain: LH stimulates theca interna cells to synthesise androgens. FSH stimulates granulosa-cell aromatase, which converts these androgens to oestrogens.

questions.q: Which pituitary hormone directly supports Sertoli-cell function and promotes production of androgen-binding protein?
questions.explain: FSH acts on Sertoli cells, supporting spermatogenesis and stimulating production of androgen-binding protein and inhibin B.
